Expeditiously means in a way that is both fast and efficient — getting something done quickly without wasting time, effort, or resources.

The key here is that it's not just about speed. It carries two ideas packed into one word:

  • Speed — without unnecessary delay
  • Efficiency — without wasting steps or effort

So when someone does something expeditiously, they're not rushing carelessly. They're moving with purposeful, smart speed — the way a skilled professional handles a task.

Think of it this way:

Imagine a doctor in an emergency room. They don't panic, they don't waste time, and they don't take longer than needed. They assess the patient and act — fast and smartly. That's expeditiously.

Or think of a well-trained waiter at a busy restaurant. They take your order, confirm it clearly, and bring your food without delay or confusion. No wasted trips, no unnecessary back-and-forth. That's acting expeditiously.
What Makes It Different From Just "Quickly"

This is an important distinction. Consider these three words:

  • Quickly → only tells you about speed. You ran quickly. You ate quickly. Simple.
  • Efficiently → only tells you about smartness — doing something without waste. No particular hurry implied.
  • Expeditiously → tells you both at once. Speed + efficiency. It's the combination that makes this word special.

A surgeon can operate quickly but make careless mistakes. A surgeon who operates expeditiously is both fast and precise — doing the job in the minimum time needed, correctly.

Expeditiously is a formal word. You will almost never hear it in casual conversation between friends. It lives in:

  • Legal language — "The court will handle this matter expeditiously."
  • Business and official writing — "We will process your request expeditiously."
  • Government and administrative communication — "The authorities responded expeditiously to the crisis."
  • Professional emails and reports — "Please ensure this is resolved expeditiously."

If you used it in a casual setting — say, telling a friend to "pass the salt expeditiously" — it would sound humorously over-formal. People would laugh. That tells you a lot about where it belongs.

Here are clear examples across different contexts, so you can see how it actually works in use:

  1. "The company promised to address all customer complaints expeditiously."
    → They'll handle the complaints quickly and without dragging it out unnecessarily.
  2. "The legal team worked expeditiously to file the documents before the deadline."
    → They moved fast and skillfully to get the paperwork done in time.
  3. "The relief supplies were delivered expeditiously to the flood-affected region."
    → Aid reached the people quickly, with no time wasted in logistics.
  4. "She handled the disagreement expeditiously, resolving it in one short meeting."
    → She dealt with it fast and effectively — no dragging it out.
  5. "The government acted expeditiously to contain the outbreak."
    → They responded with quick, efficient action.

Notice a pattern: the word often appears with action verbs — handled, resolved, delivered, acted, processed, completed. It describes the manner in which an action is carried out.

To avoid confusion:

  • It does not mean recklessly fast or rushed. There's no carelessness in the word. The efficiency part rules that out.
  • It does not mean slowly but carefully. The speed is essential.
  • It does not mean just on time (that's more like promptly). Expeditiously implies an active drive to move fast, not merely meeting a deadline.

When you read or hear "expeditiously," it signals competence in motion. It suggests that the person or organization being described is capable, responsible, and takes the matter seriously. There's a sense of reassurance in it — like being told, "This is in good hands and won't be delayed."

It's also slightly formal and stiff, which is why it's often used by institutions, officials, or professionals to communicate seriousness and reliability.
One-Line Summary to Remember It Forever
Expeditiously = quickly + efficiently + without unnecessary delay — the word for when a capable person handles something the right way, fast.
